why: Check 2 is fine: grep plus a requirement that a line actually documents the flag matches "README.md documents --tsv". Check 1 goes further than its expect line in three places. Its PASS condition requires "exit=0", but the words only say the command reads input and prints a JSON array, not how it exits. It requires the outputs to be "byte-identical" via cmp, but "the same JSON array" would also be met by the same array with different whitespace. It also fixes the exact CSV output "(here [{\"name\":\"Ada\",...}])", which the words never specify, since they only compare against whatever the CSV run prints. The exit-code and byte-identity checks belong under Advisory, not in PASS or FAIL. The FAIL condition repeats the "exits non-zero" test. So the criterion does not hold for the whole output.
